changes: New: TRIG + SCENE. In grid recording, hold one or more trigs and press SCENE A, SCENE B or both; when you let go of the last scene key, the scene's locked values (or the crossfader's current blend) become p-locks on the held steps of the active track. Requested by an MK1 user on Discord.

One scene writes every value it locks, replacing a p-lock the step already had for that parameter and leaving the step's other p-locks alone; the blend writes what each step plays at the current fader position, using the step's own p-lock where it has one. Slots the page lacks are skipped and values stay inside each parameter's range, as stock's own p-lock writer does; the held trigs stay. Toasts: SCENE A TO TRIGS, SCENE B TO TRIGS, SCENE BLEND TO TRIGS, or NOTHING TO LOCK.

Stock gestures inside the chord keep their meaning: a trig pressed while the scene key is held selects a scene and a knob turned writes a scene lock, and then no p-lock is written. SCENE first, then a trig, still selects a scene. There is no undo; hold the trig and press PLAY (stock) to clear that step's p-locks.
Two new patch sites: the entries of stock's SCENE press and release handlers. The Part apply (SCENE + YES) is unchanged.
Tested under ot_emu only (verify.py). TRIG + SCENE has not run on hardware, on the MKII or the MK1; the card build was not run on hardware for this version.

New module: hold SCENE A or SCENE B and press YES to write that scene's locked values into the active Part as its own knob values; hold both scene keys and press YES to write the sound the crossfader blends right now. Covers SRC page 1 of the assigned machine, LFO speed and depth, AMP, FX1 and FX2 on all eight audio tracks.

The scenes, the scene selection, the mutes, the crossfader and the saved Part are not changed, so RELOAD PART (FUNC + CUE) is the undo. An apply that changes no value (no locks, the same apply twice, or the blend with both scenes muted) shows NOTHING TO APPLY.

Changes one stock gesture: YES with a scene key held no longer shows ARM ALL; YES alone still does. XVOL and XLV stay scene locks; trig locks and LFO modulation are not written. A parameter locked in only one scene can change sound after an apply.

Tested on one MKII over USB on the beta base (the contributor, by watching values, no audio check): all three modes, NOTHING TO APPLY, Keep, Undo, removal and a power cycle with the module kept, with a package that differs from the published one only in its display name (the published one was installed and kept, not run). Under ot_emu: the applied bytes equal stock's morph model, Part and project save and reload, and an emulated power cycle; under a MIDI flood it costs nothing between presses, and an apply raises the emulated frame interrupt by under 2% of a frame. Not measured: how long an apply takes on the unit; a card build on hardware was not run for this version.
Documentation note (21 Oct 2026, no package change): the module page credits the author as Nathaniel Pavel (GitHub @npp1993).
